title: Sacredness of life
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 8 Christian Religious Education; not yet checked by a CRE teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Suicide and abortion are taught for protection and hope, in the school's agreed words, with the counsellor present if possible. Name where to get help (a parent, teacher, counsellor, pastor, Childline Kenya 116). If a learner shows distress, stop and follow the safeguarding policy. These skills have no question families and should be checked in class discussion first.

skills.key_step: The learner explains the sacredness of life (life is God's gift; people are made in his image), elaborates it from the scriptures (Genesis 1:27, 2:7, 9:6; Exodus 20:13; Psalm 139:13-16; Jeremiah 1:5) and discusses how the right to life is violated today (murder, mob justice, abortion, suicide, reckless driving, drugs).

floor.prerequisite: Knows practices that violate the right to life.
floor.question: A crowd wants to beat a thief. What is right?

contexts: a family welcoming a new baby

board.do: Point at "in the image of God".
board.say: Why does this make every life sacred?

board.do: Wait for the learner to say every person bears God's image.
List violations of the right to life.

misconceptions.repair: Read Genesis 2:7 and Psalm 139:13: God gives life and forms each person.
Read Exodus 20:13 and link "do not murder" to the sacredness of life.

misconceptions.ask: What should a child do who feels hopeless?
misconceptions.repair: Name trusted adults and Childline 116; say that asking for help is brave.

listen_for: Only good people's lives are sacred
misconceptions.ask: Why is every human life sacred, according to Genesis 1:27 and 9:6?
misconceptions.repair: Read Genesis 9:6: because God made people in his image, every life is protected.

skills.key_step: The learner names causes of suicide and of abortion among teenage girls, analyses the consequences of violating the right to life, compiles values and life skills that uphold it (hope, seeking help early, empathy, self-esteem, chastity, communication), and names where to get help, in the school's agreed words and with care.
representations: a "help circle": parent, teacher, counsellor, pastor, Childline 116
steps: Name what can make people feel hopeless.
Compile values and say where to get help.

board.do: Draw a help circle with five names.

board.say: A friend feels hopeless. What do you do?

board.do: Wait for the learner to say listen and tell a trusted adult.
Write the values and life skills around the circle.

listen_for: Say nothing and change the subject
misconceptions.ask: A friend says she feels life is not worth living. What should you do?
misconceptions.repair: Teach: listen, take it seriously, do not keep it secret, tell a trusted adult now. Name Childline 116.

listen_for: No, only weak people feel that way
misconceptions.ask: Can a strong Christian feel hopeless?
misconceptions.repair: Read 1 Kings 19:4-8: Elijah asked to die, and God gave him rest, food and care. Seeking help is wise.

misconceptions.ask: Name one consequence of unsafe abortion for a teenage girl.
misconceptions.repair: List health, emotional, spiritual and legal consequences; teach compassion and where to get help.

misconceptions.ask: Which of these violates the right to life?
misconceptions.repair: Make a list with the class and link each to the sacredness of life (Genesis 1:27; Exodus 20:13).

checks.question: A friend says life is not worth living. What do you do?
checks.answer: Listen, take it seriously and tell a trusted adult at once

checks.question: Name a value or life skill that upholds life.
